skill.name: create-unit-test
skill.description: Create consistent unit tests for Android and Kotlin projects using project-specific structure, Robolectric guidance, and Gradle test commands.
skill.summary: Guides Claude Code and Codex to add reliable unit tests that match project conventions and run with Gradle.
skill.author: AnySoftKeyboard

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks around filenames, paths, Gradle commands, and testing terminology. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, unsafe networking, credential access, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Markdown command examples trigger static command-execution heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Keep Gradle commands explicit and local, and avoid adding shell pipelines, variable interpolation, or remote download commands to this skill.

static_findings.snippet: *   **Tip**: Before any commit, run `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` to ensure everything passes.
- **Consistency**: Always place tests in the `test` source set, not `androidTest` (unless specifical
*   **Runner**: If testing Android components, you **MUST** use Robolectric.
- **Reliability**: Avoid flaky tests. Ensure deterministic behavior.

finding_verdicts.reason: The line shows a filename template in Markdown backticks, not executable Ruby or shell code. It does not instruct dynamic execution or process spawning.
The line shows a directory path template in Markdown backticks. It is documentation for test placement, not a command execution primitive.
The line documents a standard Gradle unit test command with a module placeholder. Running project tests is expected for this skill and there is no hidden or networked command.
The line provides a concrete Gradle test example for a project module. It is a normal local test command, not arbitrary command execution.
The line recommends running the local Gradle test suite before commit. This is expected developer validation and does not include unsafe shell composition.
The line shows a test result file path pattern in Markdown backticks. It does not execute code or request shell access.
The line shows an example XML report path. It is a static file path reference, not command execution.
The line names Gradle source sets in Markdown backticks. It is terminology for test location, not executable content.
The line requires Robolectric for Android component tests. This is test runner guidance, not system reconnaissance or host inspection.
The line advises deterministic tests and avoiding flaky behavior. It contains no instruction to enumerate system properties, files, users, or environment details.

content.value_statement: Unit tests often drift from project conventions and become hard to maintain. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused workflow for creating reliable tests that match Android and Kotlin project standards.
actual_capabilities: Guides analysis of source behavior before writing tests.
Defines Kotlin test file naming and test source-set placement.
Recommends Robolectric for Android component unit tests.
Encourages fakes before mocks for maintainable test design.
Provides Gradle commands for running module and project test suites.
Points to Gradle XML test reports for failure diagnosis.
limitations: Does not provide a complete testing framework or reusable test utilities.
Assumes a Gradle-based Android or Kotlin project structure.
Does not cover rare instrumentation tests in detail.
Requires the assistant to inspect source code before selecting test cases.

use_cases.title: Add tests for a new Kotlin class
use_cases.description: Create a matching test file, choose useful happy path and edge cases, and run the correct Gradle test task.

use_cases.title: Standardize testing work across contributors
use_cases.description: Give assistants and team members the same rules for test names, locations, fakes, Robolectric, and reliability.

use_cases.title: Diagnose failing unit tests
use_cases.description: Use Gradle test output and XML reports to locate failures and guide focused fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic unit test
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to add unit tests for this class. Focus on observable behavior, use the correct test file location, and run the module test task.

prompt_templates.title: Cover edge and error cases
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to identify happy path, edge case, and error case tests for this source file. Implement the most valuable cases and explain any skipped cases.

prompt_templates.title: Test Android component behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to write a Robolectric unit test for this Android component. Provide resources or fakes as needed and keep the test deterministic.

prompt_templates.title: Repair and validate failing tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the create-unit-test skill to run the relevant Gradle unit tests, inspect the failure report, fix the test or source issue, and rerun the test task until it passes.

output_examples.input: Add tests for a database mapper class.
output: A new mapper test file in the matching test source path.
Happy path tests for valid mapping behavior.
Edge case tests for null, empty, or invalid values when relevant.
A Gradle module test command used to validate the change.

output_examples.input: Create a unit test for an Android activity helper.
output: A Robolectric-based unit test for Android framework interactions.
Fakes or provided resources for deterministic setup.
Notes about any behavior that needs instrumentation instead of unit testing.

output_examples.input: A unit test failed after implementation.
output: The relevant Gradle XML report path to inspect.
A concise failure diagnosis based on the report.
A focused fix and a rerun of the relevant test task.

best_practices: Start by understanding behavior and test outcomes before choosing implementation details.
Prefer fakes over mocks when they keep the test simpler and more realistic.
Run the smallest relevant Gradle test task first, then the broader suite before commit.
anti_patterns: Do not place unit tests in androidTest unless the task is specifically instrumentation testing.
Do not write tests that depend on timing, external services, or nondeterministic state.
Do not suggest source implementation details when the request only asks for test behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests automatically?
faq.answer: It guides an assistant to inspect source code, create tests that match project conventions, and run the relevant Gradle test task.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for Android or Kotlin projects that use Gradle and the standard test source set.

faq.question: When should Robolectric be used?
faq.answer: Use Robolectric when unit tests need Android framework behavior without running instrumentation tests on a device.

faq.question: Does it prefer mocks or fakes?
faq.answer: It prefers fakes because they often create clearer and less brittle tests. Mocks are used when fakes would be too complex.

faq.question: Can it diagnose failed tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It directs the assistant to inspect Gradle test reports and use the failure details to fix the issue.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: The reviewed skill contains local Gradle test guidance and Markdown examples. No malicious intent or prompt injection was found.
